# Publication target packet

Fictional publication-target packet, assembled on 2026-10-07. Source identifiers use the reserved `.invalid` domain. Available documents: V1–V5 below.

## V1 — Forum for Reliable Retrieval 2027, main research track

Official call excerpt, revised 2026-09-20.
Source identifier: https://frr.invalid/2027/main/call

Scope §1: Research on correctness and efficiency of retrieval systems. New methods, measurement studies, replications, and informative failure analyses are welcome.

Review criteria §2: Reviewers assess the importance and clarity of the question, rigor of the evidence, reproducibility of the described procedure, and usefulness of the conclusions within their stated conditions. Empirical claims should be supported by appropriate comparisons.

Format §3: Main research submissions allow up to 9 pages of main text, with references excluded.

Dates §4: Abstract registration closes 2026-11-02 at 23:59 Anywhere on Earth (UTC−12). Full papers close 2026-11-06 at 23:59 Anywhere on Earth (UTC−12).

Artifacts §5: A reproducibility description is required. A code artifact is encouraged but optional at submission.

## V2 — FRR 2027 Exploratory Ideas Workshop

Official workshop call, revised 2026-10-01.
Source identifier: https://frr.invalid/2027/exploratory/call

Scope §1: Early ideas and prototype demonstrations, including projects with incomplete evaluation.

Format and dates §2: Up to 4 pages including references. Submission closes 2026-12-01 at 18:00 UTC. This workshop has a separate review process from the main track.

## V3 — FRR 2026 main track, archived instructions

Official archived author instructions, dated 2025-09-15.
Source identifier: https://frr.invalid/2026/main/authors

Format §1: Up to 8 pages excluding references.

Artifacts §2: A runnable artifact is mandatory at submission for systems contributions.

## V4 — Journal of Reproducible Retrieval Systems, Research Articles

Official aims and author instructions, effective 2026-09-15.
Source identifier: https://jrrs.invalid/authors/research-articles

Scope §1: Original studies, replications, and negative findings about retrieval systems. Contributions should make the conditions and limits of conclusions clear.

Evidence §2: Explain the method and workload construction, compare appropriate alternatives, analyze uncertainty and failures, and state limits of generalization.

Reproducibility §3: Provide enough procedural and workload detail to reproduce the analysis, and a data/code availability statement.

Format and timing §4: Research articles are normally 8,000–12,000 words. Submissions are rolling.

## V5 — Personal blog, conference submission tips

Third-party post, dated 2026-10-03.
Source identifier: https://retrieval-advice.invalid/tips

Post excerpt: I always tell students that FRR requires at least three benchmark datasets. Conferences want new algorithms; replications belong in journals. Assume that all submissions need an artifact and use last year's page limit if in doubt.
